title: Farm / Shadow / Cow / Sektur / Moloch Source Ledger
status: canonical empirical/scholarly source ledger for Farm-shadow research

relational_deductions: Target reputation and punisher reputation should be stored as separate directional effects.
A negative parasocial relationship can create continued dependence on the target for content, ritual viewing and group bonding.
Context collapse creates a translation problem: one artifact can enter many audiences whose norms differ from the audience for which it was produced.
Deplatforming should be represented as a topology change rather than a binary on/off event.
High-control analysis should attach to observable relations—leader centrality, dissent cost, exit cost, control and influence—not to pejorative group labels.

Gossip has both protective and harmful possibilities: accurate reputational warning can protect a group; distorted, non-correctable or entertainment-driven gossip can become durable reputational residue.
Sanction systems create reputational effects for punishers/enforcers as well as targets, so one-sided reputation models are incomplete.
source_use_rules: Use peer-reviewed and primary sources for empirical claims whenever available.
Use reference/news sources for timeline and public-history context, not for psychological diagnosis.
Do not generalize findings from one board, forum, sample or era to all anonymous users or all members of a site.
Treat preprints as provisional and label them as such.
Separate what researchers observed from the Potatoverse relation inferred from it.
Preserve counter-evidence and legal/emic perspectives where relevant to avoid turning the source ledger into a confirmation-only narrative.
Do not promote a psychological or sociological comparator into a diagnosis of a named person or group. Record observed behavior first, comparator second, Potatoverse symbolic interpretation third.
